what_differs: On page 437 the document gives 18 bilateral social security agreements, 16 of them with EU Member States, and a few lines later 20 international agreements, 17 of them with EU Member States; the list that follows names 18 states. Item -0495 elsewhere in the document also gives 17 agreements with EU Member States.
The staffing of the Cyber Security Agency is given as 24 employed of 44 planned posts (page 664), 24 employed against a ceiling of 45 (page 678) and 20 of 45 posts filled (page 1356).

The narrative on page 669 gives a total cost of 613 million lei, while Annex B action 17, as recorded in the item's extraction note, gives 615,000 thousand lei (203,000 state budget, 187,000 external, 225,000 uncovered); the uncovered share of 225 million lei is the same in both.

Page 426 states that EU citizens, like other foreigners, must obtain a temporary residence permit for work in order to be employed, while page 428 states that EU citizens have free access to all jobs except public functions that expressly require Moldovan citizenship.

The NIS 2 Directive is said to have been transposed by Law 48/2023 and Government Decision 562/2025 (page 127), while other chapters say Law 48/2023 transposed only some of its articles (page 582) or only partially harmonises the national framework with it (page 677).

Annex B action 11 sets June 2026 as the deadline for the geographical survey of broadband network coverage, while the regulator's comment in the consultation synthesis gives a deadline of 30 December 2030 under Article 27 of Law 72/2025.

The consultation synthesis deletes the action to establish the platform for cyber incident management and information exchange because it has already been carried out, while the narrative on page 680 says the platform is being created.
The Government Decision on procedures for access to employment measures is cited as No. 1276/2018 on pages 431 and 593 but as No. 1276/2016 on page 594.
The amendments to Laws No. 411/1995 and 1585/1998 for the EHIC are planned for 2025/2026 in one place and for 2026 in the other.
The tables give 310 registrations of workers posted for up to 90 days in 2025, while the running text gives 215 self-declarations covering 312 foreigners.
The extensions table gives 0 extensions for nationals of EU member states in 2025, while Romania appears among the top countries for extensions with 194.
The running text gives 229 temporary residence decisions for other purposes in 2025, while the table that follows gives 205.
The draft says the law enters into force three months after publication except Art. I point 21, while the consultation table (accepted by the author) proposes 12 months except Art. I point 19.
The brief gives 34 percent of refugees in paid work since arrival in one place and 29 percent in others.
The brief gives 77 percent of refugees with vocational or higher qualifications in one place and 76 percent in another.
Nearly half of job seekers cite insufficient Romanian as their main barrier in one place, against 36 percent in two others.
Law No. 180/2008 on labour migration is presented as the main law in force in one place and as repealed and merged into Law No. 200/2010 in another.
The share of government-to-business services digitalised is 78% in the main findings, close to 80% in the economic section and 82% as of June 2026 in Chapter 10.
Pages 9 and 99 give 718 mapped services with 276 digital, while page 96 gives 714 mapped (mid-August 2023) with 283 digital.
Corporate income tax declarations are said to be mandatorily digital, yet only 81% of businesses declared corporate income tax digitally for 2022; possibly different groups of taxpayers.
The report gives 714 services with 283 e-services (attributed to AGE) and 523 services with 226 digitalised, 43.2% (attributed to MDED).
The number of CUPS is 103 in para. 75, 104 as the 2023 baseline in Table 3, and 85 in 2023 and 104 in 2024 according to the State Chancellery.
Table 3 sets a target of 150 CUPS while the document cites the National Development Plan 2025-2027 target of 100 functional CUPS by 2027.
The share of citizens able to use e-services independently is 39.4% in 2024 in para. 17 and 40.5% in the explanatory note.
The EGDI baseline is position 79 with target 70 in Table 16, but position 70 with target 64 in Table 15, and para. 72 gives 70th in 2024.
The 2023 figures (3,058,794 online and 1,310,332 at the counter) do not add up to the stated total of 4,524,731; the 2024 figures (5,187,261 and 847,340) differ from the total of 6,034,611 by 10.

The programme says only 10% of portal services can be obtained with qualified trust services, while the e-Governance Agency's response says this does not correspond to reality and gives 303 of 648 services online.
Of the same 648 portal services, 303 are said to be available online after authentication and 301 accessible with a digital identity; possibly different measures.

The baseline share of public services accessed online by individuals is 30% in Table 3, while para. 18 gives G2C online requests at 41% in the first three quarters of 2024; possibly different reference periods.
70% of G2B requests are said to be online, but 2.48 million of 3.7 million is 67%, and 2.48 million online plus 1.1 million in person does not make 3.7 million.

Page 24 says there is no system for online registration of commercial entities or CSOs, while page 24 also says commercial registration has an automated system and page 19 says registration documents can be submitted electronically.

The summary refers to the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, the Chapter 10 section to a National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2027 (the 2025-2027 document is the Implementation Programme).
Page 3 says 36 of 157 public services that can be requested online are fully digital, page 4 that 226 of 523 services are digitalised (possibly different definitions).
All ARCOM permits are said to be 100% digitalised through SIA GEAP, but only 109 of 303 technical permits in 2025 were issued through it (online filing began on 7 July 2025).

Chapter 10 (pages 14 and 70) says the Cybersecurity Agency was established in December 2023, while Chapter 31 (page 90) says Moldova launched the National Agency for Cyber Security in February 2024; possibly establishment versus launch.
The data protection authority says it issued 347 decisions, but the breakdown it gives (266 with no violation and 173 with violations) adds up to 439.
The situation analysis says the Cyber Security Agency acts as the national CERT, while the indicator table gives a baseline of 0 for a functional national CERT.
5G population coverage is given as 25 to 40% (page 69, citing the European 5G Observatory) and as 25 to 35% (page 87).
The deadline for transposing the EU AI Act is given as by 2027 (PNA proposals) and as by the end of 2026 on the same page 685.
Electronic communications staffing in the MDED directorate is given as 5 persons (page 672) and as 4 persons with 1 vacant unit (page 669).

Share of the population with 100 Mbps connectivity is given as 14% with a 60% target (Table 5) and as 37.8% with a 50% target (Table 16); the regulator's recalculation gives 26.3% for 2022 and 37.8% for 2023.
Average fixed broadband download speed is given as 122 Mbps (paragraph 21 and Table 5) and as 106 Mbps (explanatory note, page 68).

Household internet access is given as 825.2 thousand of 1.1 million households, about 75% (page 7), and as 88% of rural and 92.6% of urban households in 2023 (page 68); possibly fixed connections against any access.
The Law on electronic identification and trust services is described as broadly aligned with the EU acquis on page 86 and as partially aligned with the eIDAS Regulation on page 87.
Page 675 says reuse of public sector data is at present regulated by Law No. 305/2012, while the same page says the new Law No. 109/2025 on open data has been adopted.
The staffing table gives one person for information technology, information society and trust services, while the text says trust services are not currently covered by any ministry employee.
The Intelligence and Security Service is named as responsible for trust services policy, while elsewhere the Ministry is named, or is to become, the institution responsible for trust services policy.
EvoSign users after the August 2024 pilot launch are given as 15,450 in the text and as 8,583 up to mid-December in a consultation comment.
EvoSign is described as launched in pilot mode and officially launched and accessible, and elsewhere as at the pilot stage, not launched or put into operation.
